identity.title: HIF-1alpha regulates the proliferation and differentiation of mouse cranial base sphenoid-occipital synchondrosis chondrocytes via PI3K/Akt signaling.

content.abstract: The cranial base synchondrosis (CBS) is a critical growth center in the craniofacial region, and its abnormal development can lead to various craniofacial deformities. In a hypoxic microenvironment, hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha) is a crucial regulatory factor for cellular adaptation to low oxygen conditions. However, the role of HIF-1alpha in the CBS and its mechanisms regulating the function of chondrocytes remain unclear. This study aims to investigate the expression characteristics of HIF-1alpha in the CBS and its potential mechanisms in regulating mouse spheno-occipital synchondrosis (SOS) chondrocytes (SOSCs). Histological and immunohistochemical staining were utilized to observe the growth pattern of the SOS and the expression characteristics of HIF-1alpha in the SOS of 1-8 week-old mice. Chemical hypoxia simulation and siRNA technology modulated HIF-1alpha expression, and potential signaling pathways were detected through transcriptome sequencing. Results indicate that HIF-1alpha is expressed in all layers of the mouse SOS and is closely associated with cell proliferation and differentiation. In vitro studies demonstrate that enhancing HIF-1alpha expression enhances cell proliferation and matrix synthesis capacity, improves cell apoptosis, and enhances the expression of chondrogenic markers SOX9 and Collagen II while diminishing osteogenic marker RUNX2 expression. We found that with the upregulation of HIF-1alpha expression, the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway is activated. In conclusion, our study revealed that HIF-1alpha regulates the proliferation and differentiation of SOSCs by activating the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway.
